analysis:
This PR contains only documentation: a new changelog fragment (changelog.d/startup-shape-warmup.md, lines 1-3) and an added paragraph in docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (head lines 534-541). No executable source is supplied, so no code-level security behavior changed in the evidence.

The docs describe a startup Metal kernel shape warmup. It runs after model load and self-test, before provider registration and before the local listener opens. It reuses the existing calibration session, idle gate and foreground lease, within the same KV and service budgets. It publishes no observations or work totals and trains no rates. It is bounded to 20 seconds and has a probe skip. The proactive MLX pool sweep waits while a session runs, and on-pressure reclaims still run. It is disabled by DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP=0, and 'always' skips the probe.

Threat-model relevance:
- Availability: the warmup delays registration and listener opening by up to 20 s per model on a cold cache (5.4-7.4 s measured). This is bounded and local, not a regression.
- Memory admission (TB-007): the docs state that no extra memory allowance is created and that activation and OS reserves are unchanged. That claim cannot be verified without the implementation.
- Warmup runs synthetic prompts, not consumer data. It does not touch A-001, the prefix cache (T-041) or attestation paths in the visible docs. Whether warmup prompts could populate or donate to the SSD prefix cache is not stated; the next pass should confirm that warmup donations are disabled.
- The doc's statement that the warmup skips the posture check in the startup-preload pass relies on code not provided. The implementation would need to confirm that it cannot delay or bypass the attestation or authorization gates before registration, and that foreground requests cancel the warmup.

No findings. The implementation is not in this batch, so those contracts are unverified. They are recorded here, not reported as a vulnerability.
